question:
<Context>Self-fulfilling expectations: When we have expectations or expectations of the consequences, certain behaviors will be triggered. Expectations can form self-encourage or other people's encouragement through self-suggestion or other person's suggestion. Positive expectations produce positive results, while negative expectations produce negative results.</Context><Question>Which of the following phenomena are not "self-fulfilling expectations"?</Question><Options>(A): Her classmates say she is beautiful, and the more I look, the more I look beautiful..

(B): He was always worried that he was introverted and could not pass the interview. As a result, he was particularly nervous and was eliminated during the interview..

(C): The constellation book said that her academic studies were not smooth this year, so she was decadent and negative, and the final exam really failed..

(D): Relatives and friends praised him for being smart, and he will definitely be admitted to a prestigious university in the future. After being encouraged, he studied harder and was admitted to Peking University..
</Options>
response:
<step>
<premise>Self-fulfilling expectations: When we have expectations or expectations of the consequences, certain behaviors will be triggered.</premise>
<premise>Positive expectations produce positive results, while negative expectations produce negative results.</premise>
<conclusion>A self-fulfilling expectation requires expectations to trigger behaviors that lead to results confirming the expectations.</conclusion>
</step>

<step>
<premise>In option (A), classmates say she is beautiful, creating an expectation.</premise>
<premise>The result is "the more I look, the more I look beautiful," which is a change in the observer's subjective perception rather than an outcome produced by triggered behavior.</premise>
<conclusion>Option (A) lacks a triggered behavior that brings about the expected result; it is only a perceptual bias, not a self-fulfilling expectation.</conclusion>
</step>

<step>
<premise>In option (B), the worry about failing the interview is a negative expectation.</premise>
<premise>This worry triggers nervous behavior, which leads to elimination in the interview.</premise>
<conclusion>Option (B) is a self-fulfilling expectation.</conclusion>
</step>

<step>
<premise>In option (C), the constellation book's prediction of poor academic studies is a negative expectation.</premise>
<premise>This triggers decadent and negative behavior, leading to actual failure in the exam.</premise>
<conclusion>Option (C) is a self-fulfilling expectation.</conclusion>
</step>

<step>
<premise>In option (D), the praise and expectation of being admitted to a prestigious university is a positive expectation.</premise>
<premise>This triggers harder studying behavior, leading to admission to Peking University.</premise>
<conclusion>Option (D) is a self-fulfilling expectation.</conclusion>
</step>

<step>
<premise>Option (A) does not involve a triggered behavior producing the expected result.</premise>
<premise>Options (B), (C), and (D) all involve triggered behaviors producing expected results.</premise>
<conclusion>Therefore, the phenomenon that is NOT a "self-fulfilling expectation" is described in option (A).</conclusion>
</step>
